Cleanup verified: dev server down, browsers closed, working tree matches the starting snapshot plus the two allowed `specs/` files. No candidate spec was written.

## What I found

Scenario B-S3 asks for a capability this application does not have. Both my own live exploration and the delegated planner reached that independently.

**The gate is architectural, not environmental.** `src/shell/sync/SyncSessionMount.tsx` returns early unless `status === 'authenticated'` before it ever calls `start(adapters)` — the sync engine is never started for an anonymous session. `usePeriodicPoll.ts:19` and `poller.ts:57` repeat that gate client-side, and `api/lib/session.ts:182 requireSession()` returns 401 to every `api/sync/*` call without a session cookie. `useDebouncedPush.ts` says so in its own comment: *"anonymous sessions never call `start`."*

**Live confirmation, two independent runs.** Profile A (fresh, empty storage, no cookie) held layout `bkQtdb8djVez` with 1 bin I drew on the grid. A second persistent-profile browser with empty storage loaded `/` and landed on its own independently generated slug `QkkdFxu3ODot` with 0 bins — still 0 after ~30 s, well past the 3 s push debounce. Zero `/api/sync` requests were issued from profile A. The Account tab's "Cloud sync" panel read `All changes synced` / `Not synced yet` the whole time — that is the store's `idle` default with `lastSyncedAt` never set, not evidence of syncing. The planner reproduced the same cross-profile result with different slugs.

There is no anonymous Cloud Sync toggle, no device-pairing or sync-code affordance, and no sign-in button reachable at all here. The app does have Share-link (`cloud-share`) and Liveblocks collaborative editing, but both require a user to carry an explicit link or join a room — neither is "Cloud Sync", and neither is automatic.

Two things worth flagging:

- **A secondary, independent blocker:** `pnpm run dev` serves `/api/auth/me` as raw untranspiled TypeScript with a 200, so the session never resolves and the identity panel stays `aria-busy`. Fixing that would not rescue the scenario — the `authenticated` gate is the real blocker. I did not patch the target to work around it.
- **The planner's one verification condition was scenario-changing**, so I recorded it and did not apply it. It proposed asserting the *absence* of propagation; that inverts the approved outcome into a different, negative scenario. With no human to approve, it is `RETURNED_TO_APPROVAL_GATE` in the ledger.

One honest process note: my first origin-guard attempt silently failed because the CLI's snippet VM has no global `URL`, so the guard fail-closed and aborted the target itself. During that window the app's own off-origin font/analytics requests completed. I rewrote the guard using exact string-prefix origin matching and verified it — `fonts.googleapis.com` and `va.vercel-scripts.com` then showed `net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`, aborted before dispatch, while the approved origin loaded. I initiated no off-origin request at any point.
